t: You're at Kensal Green Cemetery, which opened in 1833. It covers 72 acres beside a canal and was inspired by Père Lachaise in Paris. It has mausoleums for the rich and famous, plenty of smaller graves, three chapels, and at least 33 species of bird. It's one of London's Magnificent Seven cemeteries. Among those buried here is Charles Babbage, who originated the concept of a digital programmable computer. The novelist William Makepeace Thackeray, who wrote Vanity Fair, is here, and so is Robert Owen, a founder of the co-operative movement. Nobel winners Harold Pinter and Patrick Blackett lie here too, along with Freddie Mercury of Queen.
